entities.summary: Shimogamo Shrine  is an important Shinto sanctuary in the Shimogamo district of Kyoto city's Sakyō ward. Its formal name is Kamo-mioya Shrine . It is one of the oldest Shinto shrines in Japan and is one of the seventeen Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto which have been designated by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site. The term Kamo-jinja in Japanese is a general reference to Shimogamo Shrine and Kamigamo Shrine, the traditionally linked Kamo shrines of Kyoto; Shimogamo is the older of the pair, being believed to be 100 years older than Kamigamo, and dating to the 6th century, centuries before Kyoto became the capital of Japan.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of Japan's oldest Shinto shrines, Shimogamo Shrine played a significant role in the country's spiritual and cultural heritage for centuries. Its designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site highlights its importance to Japanese history and identity.
